newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown pledges to control finances.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown pledges to control finances.

text.p: Britain's main opposition Labour Party on Monday pledged to keep control of taxation, spending and borrowing if it wins the next election.
Economics spokesman Gordon Brown said there must be sound management of public finances.
"We're in a new world. We're in a new global economy," Brown said on BBC television.
"You've got manage public finances properly if you are going to succeed. You can't let taxation, spending and borrowing get out of control."
He added: "You must make the decisions that you've got to make so that people can have work, so that industries can prosper, so...we can be equipped for the future."
Brown is scheduled to deliver a keynote address on his party's economic plans later on Monday.
In his speech, Brown is expected to set out a tough policy on public sector pay as part of an effort to persuade voters it can be trusted to run the economy responsibly if it wins the election.
Sunday newspapers said Brown would warn Britain's six million public sector workers that Labour would extend the government's four-year freeze on their pay.
Labour enjoys an opinion poll lead of almost 20 percentage points over Prime Minister John Major's Conservatives, who must call an election by May 22.
